description:
Why do cats purr? It is not only a happy sound: NC State's vet school (2012) says cats may purr when in pain, and a Washington State University Q&A (2023) says they also purr when stressed. How the sound is made: in a 2023 lab study, voice boxes taken from 8 cats all made purr-range sound, about 25 to 30 vibrations a second, when air was passed through them, with no signal from a brain. The authors think pads of tissue in the vocal folds allow such a low sound, and they say their data do not fully rule out the older idea that brain-driven muscle twitches play a part. Experts do not yet agree on why cats purr.

#cats #catfacts #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: Herbst et al. 2023, Current Biology; NC State College of Veterinary Medicine (2012); Washington State University, Ask Dr. Universe (2023).
